newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark seen gaining foothold after slide.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark seen gaining foothold after slide.

text.p: A sizable slide in dollar/mark on Thursday is not a prelude to further damage, although technical indicators do point to a near-term consolidation at lower levels, chartists said.
"If you look at a daily chart it didn't do much damage," John Tirone, technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc, said of a drop from session highs of 1.7334 marks to an intra-session low of 1.7165.
"We're right back in the middle of a congestion area we've been in ... and for it to be positive it really has to get back above 1.7225 at a minimum," he added.
At 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, the dollar was trading hands at 1.7215/25 marks.
Good support in dollar/mark was pegged at 1.7125/30, the bottom of a rising wedge pattern which chartists said points to consolidation.
"We've been carving out a rising wedge," said David Solin, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics. "I expect a rangy top-build over the next few weeks."
Solin also put near-term resistance at 1.7225 and said a stronger ceiling lurked near 1.7325.
In dollar/yen, Tirone said a close of 126.50 would be encouraging. He predicted calls for a top at Thursday's fresh 56-month high of 127.47, but said he remained cautiously bullish.
Solin cited good support in dollar/yen at 126.10, which he termed a 62 percent retracement of the move from April 17 lows.
Ahead of Thursday's new high, he pegged resistance at 126.75, a 50 percent retracement of Thursday's retreat.
